title: Aniline resonance
back: Lone pair delocalised into the ring: aniline is a weaker base than ammonia (p$K_b$ 9.38 vs 4.75), and its ortho/para positions are very reactive.

title: Hoffmann bromamide degradation
back: The amine has one carbon fewer than the amide: use it to step down a carbon chain.

title: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
back: Gives pure primary aliphatic amines only. Cannot make aniline: aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution.

title: Diazotisation
back: Aromatic diazonium salts are stabilised by resonance but still used at once.

title: Replacing –N₂⁺
back: Nitrogen gas is lost each time; $\ce{HBF4}$ then heat gives ArF.

title: Coupling reaction
back: Product: p-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange dye; attack at the para position. With aniline (weak acid) the yellow p-aminoazobenzene forms.

title: Basicity in water
back: Balance of inductive effect, solvation by H-bonding and crowding. Gas phase: 3° > 2° > 1°.

title: Hinsberg's test
back: The primary product still has an acidic N–H, so it dissolves in alkali.

title: Why acetylate aniline first?
back: Acetylation tames the –NH₂ group: no oxidation, no anilinium ion, mainly the para product.

title: Do–Ek–Teen, Do–Teen–Ek
back: Methylamines do–ek–teen; ethylamines do–teen–ek. Ammonia comes after all of them, aniline last.

title: Boiling points of amines
back: 1° and 2° amines hydrogen-bond through N–H; 3° cannot. N–H···N bonds are weaker than O–H···O, so amines boil below alcohols.

title: Why no Friedel–Crafts on aniline
back: Aniline is a base and binds the Lewis acid catalyst; the N becomes positive and deactivates the ring.

title: Sandmeyer vs Gattermann
back: Both replace –N₂⁺ by Cl or Br; Sandmeyer uses a copper(I) salt, Gattermann copper powder with the acid (lower yield).
